title: Function type signatures and call signatures
hook: A function type describes parameters and return value — the contract for callbacks, event handlers, and dependency injection. TypeScript checks call sites at compile time; JavaScript still passes any function at runtime.

blocks.text: A **function type** specifies parameter types and return type: `(a: string, b: number) => boolean`. **Call signatures** in interfaces describe callable objects: `interface Search { (query: string): Result[]; label: string; }`. **Construct signatures** type `new` expressions. Function types are **structural** — any function matching the shape is assignable. They **erase at emit** — no runtime signature checking unlike C# delegates with reflection.

entries.plainDefinition: Callable member in an interface — object that is also a function.
Function returns undefined; callers should ignore result.
Function params checked contravariantly — safer callbacks.

blocks.text: Higher-order functions (map, filter, middleware) need precise callback types. Loose `Function` or `(...args: any[]) => any` disables checking. C# `Action<T>` and `Func<T,TResult>` are named delegate types; TypeScript uses inline or alias function types. Interviewers ask about **parameter variance** on callbacks — strictFunctionTypes makes param types contravariant.

blocks.title: Prefer named type aliases
blocks.body: type EventHandler = (e: MouseEvent) => void — reuse across components instead of repeating inline.

items.title: Type alias
items.body: type Compare = (a: number, b: number) => number;

items.title: Optional and rest params
items.body: Included in the signature for full assignability.

items.title: Return type inference
items.body: Omit return on implementations; explicit on public API types.

snippet.label: Failure mode — Function type
snippet.explanation: Function type disables checking. Use precise signature or generic callback types.

blocks.title: Using Function or any for callbacks
blocks.body: Defeats strictFunctionTypes benefits — always type the signature.

blocks.text: strictFunctionTypes: callback parameter positions are contravariant — (x: Dog) => void assignable to (x: Animal) => void is rejected when strict. Return types covariant. Method parameters in classes are bivariant (historical). Overloads use multiple call signatures on one implementation. For generic callbacks, infer from usage with generics on the HOF.

blocks.title: What gets you rejected
blocks.body: Cannot write a typed higher-order function. Confusing void and undefined. Not knowing strictFunctionTypes affects callbacks.

interviewTakeaways: Function types: (params) => return — structural, erased at runtime.
Call signatures type callable objects with extra properties.
60s: Type callbacks with aliases not Function. void ignores return. C# Func/Action parallel. No runtime signature enforcement.
Follow-up: method vs function type bivariance?
commonPitfalls: Weak: Function or (...args: any[]) => any for callbacks.
Weak: confusing void return with undefined type.
Strong: Named function type aliases. Explicit public API returns. strictFunctionTypes for safe HOFs.

jsTsCorrelations.note: JS functions are first-class objects — TypeScript adds compile-time signature contracts.
Callback parameter checking parallels C# delegate variance rules more closely when enabled.
